body: Northwest Bank sued North Pearl LLC, Sturgeon Development Partners and developer Vanessa Sturgeon on August 25, 2026 in Multnomah County Circuit Court, seeking to foreclose on the Premier Gear Works Building at 1715 NW 17th Avenue in Portland's Pearl District, Willamette Week reported. The suit was first reported by an independent reporter on Medium.

According to the suit, the borrowers took out a $6 million loan in 2022 that matured in March 2024 and was not repaid. The bank says the total owed is now $7.2 million, including unpaid loan payments and nearly $2 million in accrued interest. Sturgeon did not immediately respond to Willamette Week's request for comment.

Sturgeon leased the building to the City of Portland for $18,000 a month for the NW Northrup Shelter, a 200-bed overnight shelter that opened in September 2025 despite neighborhood opposition over livability concerns. The shelter was scheduled to close permanently on September 18, 2026, about a year after it opened, after neighborhood associations and nearby business owners pressed the city to close it. A spokesman for Mayor Keith Wilson said the city did not expect the suit to affect the planned closure; Willamette Week reported that it was unclear whether the case could complicate the city's lease with Sturgeon.

timeline.label: North Pearl LLC takes out a $6 million loan from Northwest Bank
Loan matures and is not repaid, the bank says
The 200-bed NW Northrup Shelter opens in the building under an $18,000-a-month city lease
Northwest Bank files its foreclosure suit in Multnomah County Circuit Court
